method: C++ source review and independent animation-model evaluation; C++ binary was not executed

verifiedCore.claim: Original Msg bytes are concatenated without a new Digest wire header
One Digest is built for a receiving sector and copied once for each resident
SendQ receives copied bytes, not the original Msg object
Physical send is separately flushed at tick end

findings.visualEvidence: Move Msg 1 and Move Msg 3 are separately born before one Digest build
findings.codeEvidence: MarkMoveDirty deduplicates a player within a tick; FlushSectorSends builds from the final state and final sector
findings.condition: If both moves belong to the same tick, the drawing cannot treat them as two independently generated movement Msgs. If they span separate ticks, those ticks flush separately.
findings.requiredClarification: Distinguish a three-already-built-Msg input example from the actual per-tick movement-production pipeline.

findings.visualEvidence: Digest S1/S2/S3 and receiving-player labels can imply per-player Digest construction
findings.requiredClarification: Label receiving-sector construction explicitly and identify one displayed resident as a representative; residents of the same sector share one constructed Digest.

findings.visualEvidence: Msg badges above S recipients are previews, but the title does not distinguish them from stored buffers
findings.requiredClarification: Mark these as recipient previews, since actual pending Msgs are held in their source sectors.

scopeNotes: Current receiver queues are correct for the three preset Msg inputs. This does not verify that those three inputs are generated by the illustrated actions in a single actual tick.
Source-sector enumeration order and per-sector insertion order are used; this example preserves its IDs 1,2,3, but global event-time order is not a general guarantee.
Sector-crossing CREATE/DELETE traffic, self recipients, pool cleanup and physical WSASend are omitted from this focused graphic.
Ring segments represent logical Msgs; the real SendQ is a byte ring, not fixed-size Msg slots.
